key_insight: For least-squares FEM with weak boundary conditions, the correct penalty scaling is h_F^{-1} on Dirichlet terms and 1 on Neumann terms, yielding mesh-independent norm and error equivalence even for indefinite elliptic problems.
engineering_relevance: This gives a reliable a posteriori error estimator and robust recovered fluxes for mixed-boundary PDEs, including when boundary conditions are only weakly satisfied or the discretization is fully discontinuous.
method: Prove norm/error equivalence in a mesh-dependent least-squares norm.
Use inverse inequalities on discrete Dirichlet traces plus stability of the continuous boundary value problem.
Extend to a discontinuous penalty formulation with h_F^{-1} weights on both jumps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytic equivalence results with mesh-independent constants and optimal convergence, rather than numerical experiments.
watch_item: Using weaker Neumann weighting (e.g., h_F) breaks the equivalence, so implementation must respect the proposed scaling to retain reliability.
paper_title: Least-Squares Finite Element Methods with Weakly Imposed Boundary Conditions: Norm and Error Equivalences, Over-Penalization, and Fully Discontinuous Discretizations
